source_caption:
When life tells you to slow down, find someone who reminds you how to live again 🚗💨

In The Intouchables (2011), a wealthy quadriplegic man hires an ex-con as his caretaker and what starts as chaos turns into one of the most heartwarming friendships ever put on screen. This scene isn’t about breaking traffic rules, it’s about breaking limits reminding us that joy sometimes comes from the most unexpected people.

In reality, the man who inspired the character of Driss was a young Algerian named Abdel. However, directors Éric Toledano and Olivier Nakache decided to alter the character’s nationality to Senegalese. The reason? They were keen on casting Omar Sy, with whom they had previously worked in Tellement Proches (2009) and were convinced he was perfect for the role. Additionally, Sy’s own background having grown up in the underprivileged suburbs of France allowed him to bring an authentic and deeply personal touch to Driss’s story.

Where do you rate The Intouchables on the scale of 10 ?

source_details.synopsis: The Intouchables (French: Intouchables, pronounced [ɛ̃tuʃablə]), also known as Untouchable in the UK, Ireland, and Scandinavia, and 1+1 in Eastern Europe, is a 2011 French buddy comedy-drama film written and directed by Éric Toledano and Olivier Nakache. It stars François Cluzet and Omar Sy. The plot of the film is inspired by the true story of Philippe Pozzo di Borgo and his French-Algerian carer Abdel Sellou, discovered by the directors in À la vie, à la mort, a documentary film. Nine weeks after its release in France on 2 November 2011, it became the second highest-grossing French film in France, after the 2008 film Welcome to the Sticks.
